data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's guard fires on the author's own mutation \u2014 if a process guard never fires on its author, it is probably a description, not a constraint.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the author's own mutations are always caught by other modules' guards at 4/4 to 6/7, the reflexive condition is not sufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 loss is due to a single oversight rather than a systematic guard design, the constraint interpretation overstates the mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is explained by module size or registry size rather than guard reflexivity, the claim is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a shown-to-fail-first installation with a non-reflexive guard still loses mutations, the condition is not necessary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The constraint relation is reflexive: a guard that only catches others' mutations describes an imagined subject, while a guard that catches the author's own mutation constrains the actual construction. The compile.py 1/9 mutation loss shows a guard that checked declared data and therefore missed added behaviour by the same author, so the test described a narrower subject than the one installed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
